data.name: Daya
data.gender_notes: Daya is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘d-y-‘, which means to guide or to lead. In Islamic context, Daya represents a guide, helper, and supporter. The name Daya carries the meaning “Guide, Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Daya usually hope their child will grow to embody guide, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of guidance and support in one's spiritual journey in Islam.
data.etymology: Daya belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guide, Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Daya total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

In Islamic culture, Daya is seen as a person who provides direction and assistance, especially during times of hardship and uncertainty. This may include spiritual guidance, moral support, or practical assistance, making the name Daya a valuable and respected one.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Daya represents a connection to the divine source of guidance. It reminds us of the importance of being guided by Allah (God) in our lives, and of the inherent value in being a source of guidance and support for others. The name Daya serves to remind us that we are all interconnected, and that our actions and choices can have a powerful impact on those around us. It is a reminder to be compassionate, understanding, and supportive to others and to strive towards being a good leader and helper in our own lives and in the lives of those around us.
